               OpSource HLSL 600 %3 "//==========================================================================//
// This is a minimal restatement of #4486. Both loop levels carry [unroll] and
// every bound is a compile-time constant: j runs 0..2 and k runs 0..(3-j-1), so
// the whole nest is six comparisons.
//
// What to look for, per pane:
//
// - SPIR-V panes (-spirv): scroll to the fragment entry point. Two structured
//   loop headers survive, each with a back-edge and a phi for its counter, and
//   only ONE float comparison inside them -- so the nest was not unrolled. Fully
//   unrolled code would have no loop header and six comparisons.
// - DXIL pane (no -spirv): the same source has no loop at all; the comparisons
//   are materialised in straight-line code. Same shader, same attributes, two
//   different answers.
//
// Note CE builds Release binaries and appends its own debug-info flags to DXC
// panes, so the embedded source you can see in the output is CE's doing, not the
// shader's.
//==========================================================================//

// #4486, minimal restatement: nested [unroll] `for` loops with compile-time
// constant bounds, no textures, no samplers, no helper functions.
//
// Agent-constructed, not from the thread. It exists so the finding can be read
// in a few lines of SPIR-V and shown on Compiler Explorer; repro.hlsl stays the
// faithful evidence. Same loop nest as repro.hlsl (j < 3, k < 4 - j - 1) over
// the same bubble-sort body.
//
// Expectation: match.

float4 g_in;

float4 PS_bright_pass( float4 pos : SV_POSITION ) : SV_Target0
{
        float v[4] = { g_in.x, g_in.y, g_in.z, g_in.w };

        [unroll]
        for ( int j = 0; j < (4 - 1); j++ )
        {
                [unroll]
                for ( int k = 0; k < (4 - j - 1); k++ )
                {
                        [flatten]
                        if ( v[k] > v[k + 1] )
                        {
                                float tmp = v[k];
                                v[k] = v[k + 1];
                                v[k + 1] = tmp;
                        }
                }
        }

        return float4( v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3] );
}

!26 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// This is a minimal restatement of #4486. Both loop levels carry [unroll] and\0A// every bound is a compile-time constant: j runs 0..2 and k runs 0..(3-j-1), so\0A// the whole nest is six comparisons.\0A//\0A// What to look for, per pane:\0A//\0A// - SPIR-V panes (-spirv): scroll to the fragment entry point. Two structured\0A//   loop headers survive, each with a back-edge and a phi for its counter, and\0A//   only ONE float comparison inside them -- so the nest was not unrolled. Fully\0A//   unrolled code would have no loop header and six comparisons.\0A// - DXIL pane (no -spirv): the same source has no loop at all; the comparisons\0A//   are materialised in straight-line code. Same shader, same attributes, two\0A//   different answers.\0A//\0A// Note CE builds Release binaries and appends its own debug-info flags to DXC\0A// panes, so the embedded source you can see in the output is CE's doing, not the\0A// shader's.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// #4486, minimal restatement: nested [unroll] `for` loops with compile-time\0A// constant bounds, no textures, no samplers, no helper functions.\0A//\0A// Agent-constructed, not from the thread. It exists so the finding can be read\0A// in a few lines of SPIR-V and shown on Compiler Explorer; repro.hlsl stays the\0A// faithful evidence. Same loop nest as repro.hlsl (j < 3, k < 4 - j - 1) over\0A// the same bubble-sort body.\0A//\0A// Expectation: match.\0A\0Afloat4 g_in;\0A\0Afloat4 PS_bright_pass( float4 pos : SV_POSITION ) : SV_Target0\0A{\0A\09float v[4] = { g_in.x, g_in.y, g_in.z, g_in.w };\0A\0A\09[unroll]\0A\09for ( int j = 0; j < (4 - 1); j++ )\0A\09{\0A\09\09[unroll]\0A\09\09for ( int k = 0; k < (4 - j - 1); k++ )\0A\09\09{\0A\09\09\09[flatten]\0A\09\09\09if ( v[k] > v[k + 1] )\0A\09\09\09{\0A\09\09\09\09float tmp = v[k];\0A\09\09\09\09v[k] = v[k + 1];\0A\09\09\09\09v[k + 1] = tmp;\0A\09\09\09}\0A\09\09}\0A\09}\0A\0A\09return float4( v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3] );\0A}\0A"}
